title: Tender/RFQ Finder + Bid Drafter
one_liner: Agent that watches PPIP and county portals for matching Kenyan tenders and drafts compliant bid documents from your company profile.
pain_description: Kenyan SMEs and contractors must manually scan tenders.go.ke plus 47 county portals to find relevant tenders; PPIP has no alert system and most bids need paid access to RFP documents. The top bid-rejection reasons (late submission, expired tax compliance certificate, wrong tender security, missing addendum) are pure process failures, and even experienced bidders routinely miss high-value opportunities.

score_rationale.pain: Manual multi-portal scanning plus document assembly is done weekly and hated; process failures disqualify otherwise-solid bidders.
score_rationale.differentiation: Aggregators (KenyaTenders, Jorpex) sell alerts, but none draft the bid or enforce the compliance checklist from a company profile.

agent_scope: One agent fixed to the tender-discovery + first-draft workflow: daily scan of PPIP/county feeds against a company profile, then draft the technical/financial bid skeleton with a compliance checklist (tax compliance cert, tender security, AGPO flags, addenda).

title: M-Pesa Statement Reconciliation for SMEs
one_liner: Agent that matches daily M-Pesa statements against receipts and invoices and produces a clean month-end book.
pain_description: M-Pesa is the business bank account for most Kenyan SMEs, but payments arrive with no reference linking them to invoices and owners download statements weekly to tag them manually in spreadsheets. FSD Kenya and Safaricom's 2024 MSME outlook found most small firms run manual, paper-intensive collection processes that are slow, unreliable and costly; accountants then spend days reconciling month-end.

score_rationale.pain: Weekly manual matching of statements to receipts is exactly the hated recurring workflow the rubric's 5 describes.
score_rationale.differentiation: Generic accounting suites exist; few nail M-Pesa statement semantics (no invoice references, till/paybill namespaces).

agent_scope: One agent fixed to the statement-to-ledger workflow: ingest M-Pesa statement export plus receipt photos, fuzzy-match payments to invoices, flag unmatched items, emit a monthly reconciliation report and supplier payment schedule.

title: Chama Contribution & Payout Tracker
one_liner: Agent that reads M-Pesa contributions, updates the chama ledger, and posts member balances and payout schedules to WhatsApp.
pain_description: Chama treasurers reconcile member contributions by hand: check the M-Pesa statement, write the book, update a WhatsApp group. Partial payments, late payers and rotating-payout (merry-go-round) turns live in notebooks and screenshots, disputes are routine, and meetings are consumed by bookkeeping.

score_rationale.pain: Manual bookkeeping every meeting, with named pain from chama banking products themselves.
score_rationale.differentiation: MyChama and ChamaPro exist; differentiation is the agent handling partials/turn-swaps over WhatsApp rather than a portal.

agent_scope: One agent fixed to the treasurer workflow: match incoming M-Pesa payments to members (handling partials), update the shared ledger, send weekly WhatsApp balance digests and schedule payout turns.

title: Landlord Rent Tracker + Arrears Chaser
one_liner: Agent that matches rent M-Pesa payments to tenants, issues receipts, and chases arrears automatically.
pain_description: Small Kenyan landlords track rent in WhatsApp threads and notebooks; M-Pesa payments arrive without tenant references, receipts are sent manually or not at all, and arrears surface late. Market sources estimate up to 30% of rental income leaks to poor tracking and reconciliation across M-Pesa, bank and agent channels.

score_rationale.pain: Real monthly pain and revenue leakage, but less acute than the weekly-hate workflows scored 5.
score_rationale.differentiation: Rent SaaS exists (Pangoni, MyLandlord, Silqu); the agent's arrears-chasing and reconciliation angle is the wedge.

agent_scope: One agent fixed to the rent-roll workflow: match payments to units, auto-send receipts, produce a weekly arrears report with polite chase messages and a monthly landlord statement.

title: eTIMS Compliance Assistant for Small Sellers
one_liner: Agent that turns daily sales into compliant eTIMS tax invoices, including buyer-issued reverse invoices for sub-KES-5M sellers.
pain_description: eTIMS is mandatory for anyone carrying on business in Kenya and non-compliance risks penalties of KES 1M or ten times the tax; small sellers face technical glitches, complex interfaces and no capacity to integrate accounting software. The reverse-invoicing guidelines push compliance work onto purchasers, and accountants report SMEs lack the systems to keep up.

score_rationale.pain: Mandatory statutory workflow with financial penalties — compliance is repeated per sale and feared.
score_rationale.buildability: KRA system-to-system integration is heavy; eTIMS Lite/browser fallback keeps a two-week demo feasible, hence 3 not lower.

agent_scope: One agent fixed to the daily-invoice workflow: capture sales from SMS/WhatsApp/CSV, generate eTIMS-compliant invoices and receipts via eTIMS Lite with browser fallback, and assemble the buyer-issued reverse-invoice pack for small suppliers.

title: SME Credit-Readiness Pack
one_liner: Agent that cleans up an SME's M-Pesa and bank records into lender-ready financial statements and a document checklist.
pain_description: Banks reject or discourage Kenyan SME loan applicants because they cannot present accounts in an analysable form; record-keeping gaps are a documented barrier to finance and 11% of Kenyan SMEs are fully financially constrained. Owners spend days pulling statements and still get rejected on documentation.

score_rationale.pain: High-stakes but episodic (per loan application), so 4 rather than a weekly-hate 5.
score_rationale.showcase: The output is documents rather than a visually obvious live demo.

agent_scope: One agent fixed to the loan-application workflow: ingest 12 months of statements and receipts, clean and categorise, produce a financial summary pack plus per-lender document checklist.

title: Matatu SACCO Cash Accounting
one_liner: Agent that reconciles matatu SACCO daily collections from cash and M-Pesa against crew remittances.
pain_description: Matatu SACCOs lose revenue to untracked daily collections; crew remittances stay informal and documented cash-management weaknesses depress SACCO financial performance.

score_rationale.buildability: Needs field data capture at the stage; no public or simulatable data source for stage-level collections.

agent_scope: Blocked: would need physical/field collection data the current stack cannot capture within two weeks.

title: Job Application Tracker for Kenyan Youth
one_liner: Agent that tracks a job seeker's applications across Kenyan boards and drafts tailored CVs per posting.
pain_description: Kenyan youth mass-apply across fragmented job boards with no tracking, and over 75% of the population is under 35 facing limited opportunities. The workflow pain is per-application polish rather than a hated weekly task.

score_rationale.pain: Real market failure but the per-application workflow is not a weekly hated manual process.
score_rationale.differentiation: BrighterMonday/LinkedIn dominate discovery and the fleet already runs a personal job-scout lane.

agent_scope: Would overlap existing job platforms and the fleet's jobscout lane; no natural payment-rails fit.

title: SME Compliance Calendar & Penalty Shield
one_liner: Agent that tracks every Kenyan SME statutory deadline (PAYE, NSSF, SHIF, housing levy, VAT/TOT, county permit renewals) and pushes WhatsApp reminders with filing steps before each date.
pain_description: Kenyan SMEs juggle two deadline clusters every month: payroll obligations (PAYE, NSSF, SHIF, Affordable Housing Levy) due by the 9th, and VAT/Turnover Tax returns by the 20th, plus annual returns and county single-business-permit renewals. The most common reason businesses pay penalties is not aggressive tax planning but simply missed deadlines; a missed KRA filing draws automatic penalties (e.g. the higher of KES 20,000 or 5% of tax due plus 1% monthly interest) and a blocked Tax Compliance Certificate, which in turn blocks tenders, licence renewals and bank facilities. Today this lives in an accountant's head, a wall calendar, or nothing at all.

score_rationale.pain: Missed statutory deadlines trigger automatic penalties and block the Tax Compliance Certificate every month for every employer; sources frame missed deadlines as the top penalty cause, so the weekly-hate anchor fits.
score_rationale.market: Every registered employer and SME in Kenya qualifies, but firms without employees or VAT registration need a smaller subset, so 4 not 5.
score_rationale.payments: KRA/NSSF/SHA payments are naturally made via mobile money and a subscription for the service fits M-Pesa billing, but the workflow itself is reminders-and-filing rather than collection, so 4.
score_rationale.data: All deadlines are public and stable (KRA, NSSF, SHA, county calendars) and demo data is simulatable; the catch is county permit renewal dates vary by county with no API, so 4.
score_rationale.buildability: A deadline engine over public calendars plus WhatsApp reminder sequences and an iTax browser-assist is comfortably a two-week demo; full filing automation is out of scope by design.
score_rationale.differentiation: Tax agents and general calendar tools exist, but no common Kenyan SaaS agent owns the whole statutory cluster plus county permits with WhatsApp nudges, so 4.
score_rationale.showcase: A live demo showing an approaching 9th-cluster deadline, the penalty at risk, and the auto-sent WhatsApp pack is tangible but less flashy than a payment dashboard, so 4.

agent_scope: One agent fixed to the statutory-deadline workflow: build the SME's obligation calendar (9th payroll cluster, 20th VAT/TOT cluster, annual return, county permit renewal), send WhatsApp reminders with a per-deadline checklist and penalty-at-risk summary, and log confirmations.

title: Freelance Invoice Chaser & Payment Tracker
one_liner: Agent that issues Kenyan invoices with M-Pesa/Paystack payment links, matches incoming M-Pesa payments to invoices, and runs a polite automated escalation ladder for overdue ones.
pain_description: Kenyan freelancers finish the work and then wait: platforms hold payments in escrow for days, direct clients pay late, and chasing an overdue invoice is emotionally draining and relationship-risky, so many freelancers simply never chase. Guides describe chasing late payments as one of the worst parts of freelancing and the 'emotional tax' of the work. Payments that do arrive land in M-Pesa with no reference, leaving the freelancer to match them to invoices by hand.

score_rationale.pain: Every invoice carries the chase dread and Kenya-specific payout holds compound it; sources describe the pain as constant and hated, matching the weekly-hate anchor.
score_rationale.market: Kenya is a major freelancing hub for Upwork/remote work and direct-client creatives, but the buyer is one individual at a time, so 4 not 5.
score_rationale.payments: Payment is the workflow itself: M-Pesa/Paystack payment links on invoices and statement matching are the natural core, so 5.
score_rationale.data: All data is the user's own invoices and M-Pesa statement export, matched with fuzzy logic and simulatable for the demo; no public dataset needed, so 4.
score_rationale.buildability: Invoice store plus statement matching plus a scheduled WhatsApp/email escalation ladder is a two-week demo; deeper platform-API escrow tracking stays out of scope, so 4.
score_rationale.differentiation: Global invoicing tools exist (GoCardless, Wave) but nothing Kenya-native ties invoice to M-Pesa statement matching with an automated polite chaser, so 4.
score_rationale.showcase: Aging-invoice dashboard, matched payments lighting up, and an auto-sent polite chaser thread is a visually obvious demo with strong portfolio weight, so 5.

agent_scope: One agent fixed to the get-paid workflow: generate invoices with M-Pesa/Paystack links, match incoming statement lines to invoices, and send a scheduled escalation ladder (friendly nudge, firm reminder, final notice) over WhatsApp/email until paid.

title: Short-Let Turnover & Guest Ops Coordinator
one_liner: Agent that reads booking calendars, schedules cleaner turnovers over WhatsApp, and drafts guest check-in/check-out messages between tight checkout-to-checkin windows.
pain_description: Short-let hosts in Nairobi and on the Coast run a daily operations treadmill: each guest turnover triggers cleaning, inspection, restocking, key handover and guest communication inside a tight window, and a missed turnover means bad reviews and lost bookings. Diaspora and side-hustle owners run this from WhatsApp threads and phone calls, and guests message about late checkouts that desync the cleaning schedule with no unified system.

score_rationale.pain: Daily operational pain with direct revenue impact, but established co-hosts and management companies already absorb much of it, so 4 not 5.
score_rationale.market: Nairobi alone has 6,000+ active Airbnb listings and the short-let market is growing, but it is a narrower operator niche than the rubric's 5, so 4.
score_rationale.payments: Direct M-Pesa reservations are already part of the Kenyan short-let flow and a subscription fits M-Pesa, but the core workflow is coordination, not payments, so 4.
score_rationale.data: Booking data sits behind gated iCal/API access on Airbnb/Booking.com; simulatable for a demo but real integration is constrained, so 3.
score_rationale.buildability: A turnover scheduler with cleaner WhatsApp tasks and guest-message drafts is buildable in two weeks on calendar exports, so 4.
score_rationale.differentiation: Pangoni already provides Kenya-specific short-let software covering bookings, M-Pesa reservations, turnover coordination and financials, so the agent angle is thin; 2.
score_rationale.showcase: A task board turning checkout into cleaner pings and guest messages is visual, though less portfolio-distinctive given the crowding, so 4.

agent_scope: One agent fixed to the turnover window: pull upcoming bookings, assign and ping cleaners over WhatsApp with checklists, chase completion, and draft/send guest check-in and check-out messages.
